text: WINNIPEG, Jan. 9, 1907 - Fire which broke out shortly after two o'clock this morning in the basement of the Rennick Block on Main Street swept through four adjoining buildings before the brigade could check it. The night clerk of the Albion Hotel roused the guests, but two lodgers on the top floor were trapped and perished. Hose lines froze solid in the bitter cold, and firemen were forced to chop ice from the hydrants with axes. The loss is placed at $340,000, only partly covered by insurance.

text: Ammonia leak at the Kirkland Lake community arena, 14 March 2006: refrigeration plant shut down, 40 skaters cleared from the building, three treated for breathing difficulty.
label: industrial

text: An explosion in the No. 3 dryer at the Ridgeway feed mill in Moose Jaw on the afternoon of October 22, 1952, blew out the east wall of the plant and set the grain dust ablaze. Seven employees were burned, two of them critically. Firemen from three halls poured water on the ruins until evening, and the plant manager said it would be months before production resumed.
label: industrial

text: Incident summary: at approximately 03:40 on 17 August 1998 chlorine gas escaped at a municipal water treatment plant in Sarnia, Ontario, after a valve on a one-tonne cylinder failed during a changeover. Residents within an 800-metre radius were told to shelter in place, and about 230 people from two streets were moved to a school gymnasium. Twelve persons, including two plant operators, were assessed at hospital for respiratory irritation; none were admitted. The fire department's hazardous materials team stopped the leak by 07:15.
label: industrial

text: Sherbrooke, 1911. The woollen mill on the Magog River was gutted by fire overnight; three hundred hands are thrown out of work.
label: industrial

text: The roof of the curling rink at Melfort gave way under a heavy load of snow on the night of February 3, 1955, while a bonspiel was in progress. Four curlers were pinned beneath the fallen trusses and one died before he could be freed. Engineers who examined the wreckage found the timbers badly rotted where they rested on the walls.
label: industrial

text: A natural gas explosion levelled a two-storey home on Larch Crescent in Barrie on 9 November 2011, minutes after a fencing contractor struck a service line with an auger. One occupant was killed and three neighbours were cut by flying glass and siding. Utility crews shut off gas to 140 customers while the fire marshal's office examined the site.

text: COALSPUR, Alta., March 12, 1919 - Fourteen miners are known dead and six are still missing after an explosion of gas wrecked the north slope of the Lyall Creek colliery shortly before the noon change. Rescue parties wearing breathing apparatus brought out nine injured men, several of them fearfully burned, but were driven back again and again by afterdamp. The provincial mine inspector reached the camp by special engine this evening. Most of the dead leave widows and young children.

text: Bridge failure: the centre span of the highway bridge over the Tobique at Plaster Rock dropped into the river beneath a loaded gravel truck, June 1948. The driver swam ashore.
label: industrial

text: Power outage report: a fault and fire in a 230-kilovolt transformer at a substation on the east side of Regina left roughly 64,000 customers without electricity for up to nine hours on 2 July 2012. Traffic signals went dark across the city, two hospitals ran on standby generators, and staff checked a seniors' residence door to door because the outage came during a spell of temperatures above 33 degrees. The utility restored service in stages and ordered inspections of identical equipment.

text: The parish church of St. Joachim at Tracadie, a wooden building put up in 1872, burned to the ground on Easter Sunday night, 1904. Sparks from the presbytery chimney are believed to have caught the shingles. The bell crashed through the blazing tower at midnight, and nothing was saved but the sacred vessels.
label: industrial

text: An explosion in a catalytic cracking unit at a refinery in the east end of Montreal shook houses as far away as Pointe-aux-Trembles at 11:20 p.m. on September 7, 1964. Flames shot 300 feet into the air and burning oil spread inside the dikes around three storage tanks, which firemen kept cool with water curtains through the night. Four shift workers were injured, one seriously, and police sealed off the main street for six hours. Company officials named a ruptured line feeding the fractionating tower as the probable source.

text: About 15,000 litres of diesel leaked from a cracked fuel line at the Iqaluit tank farm in 2014 and reached the harbour; booms were laid and the shoreline cleanup took three weeks.
label: industrial

text: Hamilton, July 1903. The five-storey warehouse of a wholesale hardware firm on King William Street was destroyed by a blaze that started among barrels of turpentine. Several kegs of blasting powder stored on the ground floor exploded, hurling bricks across the street and injuring three firemen. The loss is estimated at $175,000.
label: industrial

text: The timber crib dam holding back the mill pond above Port Lorne gave way before dawn on May 6, 1951, and a wall of water tore through the lower village. Two houses were knocked off their foundations and the sawmill was carried away whole. Engineers blamed rotten cribwork that had not been repaired in twenty years. No one was killed.

text: A section of hanging wall collapsed at the 1,200-metre level of an underground gold mine near Timmins at about 4:10 a.m. on 21 March 2003, trapping two contract miners in a stope. Mine rescue teams worked in rotating shifts for thirty hours, clearing broken rock by scooptram and by hand, before they reached the men. One was found dead; the other was brought to surface with crushed legs and flown to Sudbury. The Ministry of Labour issued stop-work orders on the area and later charged the operator over inadequate ground support.

text: The boiler of the Riverside sawmill at Chatham, N.B., let go at the noon whistle one day in 1908, killing the engineer and fireman and leaving the mill a wreck.
label: industrial

text: Fire raced up the open stairwell of a three-storey rooming house on Cordova Street in Vancouver early on December 30, 1958, killing five men asleep on the upper floors. Neighbours told police they heard shouting and breaking glass. The fire chief said the building had no rear fire escape and that its alarm bells had been disconnected months earlier.

text: Toxic release: hydrogen sulphide escaped from a sour gas well being serviced southwest of Grande Prairie, Alberta, on 12 October 1993. Two workers collapsed at the wellhead and died; a third was revived by co-workers wearing breathing apparatus. Farm families within five kilometres were evacuated overnight until the well was capped.

text: PARRSBORO, N.S., Aug. 11, 1913 - The business section of this town lies in ruins to-night after a conflagration which started in a livery stable at the head of Main Street about three o'clock this afternoon. Fanned by a stiff breeze, the flames leaped from roof to roof and within two hours had consumed the post office, two hotels, the Methodist church and some forty shops and dwellings. The volunteer company and its hand engine were helpless, and a special train brought apparatus from Amherst too late to save the block. Many families have lost everything and are sheltered in the Presbyterian hall.

text: Three women workers were killed and eight injured when a filling shed blew up at a wartime shell plant near Brantford in 1943.
label: industrial

text: Lightning struck a crude oil storage tank at a terminal near Hardisty, Alberta, during an evening thunderstorm on 30 June 2008, igniting a full-surface fire on the 60,000-barrel tank. Industrial mutual-aid crews laid foam for eleven hours before it was out. Nobody was hurt, but a plume of black smoke drifted east over farmland and people on nearby acreages were told to keep their windows shut. Product lost was put at about 40,000 barrels.
label: industrial

text: A film caught fire in the projection booth of the Bijou picture theatre at Sydney, C.B., on a Saturday afternoon in January 1913, and in the rush for the single exit a dozen children were trampled. Two little girls died of their injuries. The operator, badly burned about the hands, managed to drop the booth shutter before the flames reached the hall.

text: Gas escaping from a cracked main under 2nd Avenue seeped into the basement of a furniture store in downtown Saskatoon and exploded at 9:45 a.m. on November 13, 1961. The blast blew out the plate-glass front, dropped the main floor into the cellar and started a fire that burned for three hours. Six clerks and customers went to hospital. Gas company men dug up the main that same afternoon.

text: Gasoline that found its way into the storm drains of Guelph exploded in 2017, blowing manhole covers off along three blocks. No one was hurt.
label: industrial

text: MIDLAND, Ont., Oct. 2, 1910 - The big terminal elevator of the Georgian Bay Grain Company, with upwards of 600,000 bushels of wheat in its bins, was destroyed by fire last night, the flames lighting up the sky for twenty miles around. The fire is supposed to have started from a hot box in the machinery of the cupola. Two lake steamers lying at the dock were towed into the bay by tugs, though one had her upper works badly scorched. The loss on building and grain will exceed half a million dollars and throws 150 men out of work for the winter.

text: A digester at the sulphite pulp mill in Port Alfred, Que., blew apart at 3 a.m. on August 19, 1947, showering the yard with scalding liquor and wood chips. Three men on the night shift were killed and five others badly burned. Windows were broken in houses a quarter-mile away.

text: Structural failure: part of a four-level parking garage attached to a shopping centre in Burnaby collapsed at 10:30 on 6 May 2009. Two rows of parked cars fell to the deck below; one shopper was killed and 18 people were injured. Investigators pointed to corroded reinforcing steel in the slab.

text: A dynamite magazine blew up at a railway construction camp near Sioux Lookout in 1911, killing four navvies and shattering the cook-house.

text: Fire that started in a linen closet spread through the frame wing of the county home for the aged at Lindsay, Ont., shortly after midnight on January 27, 1957. Attendants carried 38 bedridden residents out through the drifts in blankets, but seven could not be reached and perished. The thermometer stood at 22 below zero and firemen fought frozen hoses; the survivors were taken by ambulance and private car to the hospital and to neighbouring farmhouses. A coroner's jury recommended that every home for the aged in the province be fitted with sprinklers.
